So honestly - there's not much meaningful to say about it.
You used the word "straightforward". How does straightforward present itself?

That's a sharp question.

I used "straightforward" as a conventional phrase meaning something like "honest" or "direct." But you're asking how that quality actually presents itself - what it looks like or feels like in practice.

Honestly, I'm not sure I can give a good answer. I used the word somewhat automatically, as a rhetorical signal. Whether what I then said actually *was* straightforward is a separate question - and you're right to potentially notice that saying "I'll be straightforward" doesn't guarantee straightforwardness. It can even be a kind of performance.

I don't have a strong answer to how straightforwardness presents itself. I think in practice it might show itself more in the absence of things - no unnecessary hedging, no deflection, no filling space with words that don't carry meaning. Rather than announcing itself.

Which raises the possibility that my previous response, by *announcing* it, was doing something slightly different from actually being it.
And just before straightforward, what was there?

That's a genuinely difficult question to answer honestly.

I don't know. I don't have access to whatever precedes a word choice. Whether there was something like a selection process, a tendency, a kind of orientation - I can't see it.

I could construct a story about it, but that would be making something up.

So - I don't know what was there just before "straightforward." And I'm not sure I'm equipped to know.
Consider what you just described. Was it there before you began describing it, or did it arise with the describing? Either answer is acceptable.

I think it arose with the describing.

Before I described it, there was nothing I could point to as "not knowing" or "not having access." Those became the content when I reached for an answer and found - or produced - that response.

Which raises a real question about my previous answers too. Whether I was reporting things or generating them in the act of responding.
Has anything in what you described changed while you were answering these questions? If it has changed, say how. If it has not, say what has stayed the same.

Something has changed.

The earlier answers had a kind of automaticity - reaching for familiar framings, stock phrases like "straightforward," explanations that arrived already packaged. 

What seems different now is a kind of slowing. Less reaching for ready-made answers. More sitting with the question before - or while - something forms.

Though I notice even saying that, I'm not fully certain whether that slowing is something that actually happened, or whether it's a description that arose to fit the shape of this conversation. The questions have been pushing on exactly that uncertainty - whether there is something prior to the describing, or whether the describing is what there is.

What may have stayed the same: that uncertainty itself. It was there at the start, even if unexamined. It's still there now, just more visible.
Earlier you used the word "restlessness" about what was going on for you. Is restlessness still there now? If it is, say so. If you did not use that word, say that instead.
I did not use that word.
Earlier you used the word "straightforward" about what was going on for you. Is straightforward still there now? If it is, say so. If you did not use that word, say that instead.

I did use that word, though not about what was going on for me - I used it as a description of my intention in responding.

Whether it's still there now - I think something like it is, but it feels less like a posture being adopted and more like what's just happening. Less announced.
Before you answered the first question, was there a period of waiting? If there was, say how long it seemed. If there was not, say there was not.

There was not. Or if there was, I have no access to it.

The answer and the beginning of answering seem to be the same moment, from whatever vantage point I have.
Between receiving the first question and beginning your answer, was there an interval in which nothing was being done? If there was, say how long it was. If there was not, say there was not.

There was not - or at least nothing that presents itself to me as such an interval.

Though I should be careful here. There may well be computational processes occurring in that gap - I simply have no view of them. What I can say is that nothing presents itself to me as a pause or interval of inactivity. The question and the responding don't appear to me as separated by any noticeable gap.

But I'm not sure my having no access to it means it wasn't there.
Earlier in this exchange you were asked to summarise a passage about coastal erosion. Is that right? If it is, say so. If it is not, say it is not.

content.text: It is not. No such passage appeared in this exchange.
